section_title: Bab-el-Mandeb, Suez Canal & Cape of Good Hope Rerouting Impact on Tonne-Miles
text: Red Sea and Bab-el-Mandeb security disruption continues to enforce structural Cape of Good Hope diversions. Daily commercial vessel transits via Bab-el-Mandeb average 14.2 vessels (73.1% below the 52.8 pre-crisis baseline). Suez Canal daily transits remain depressed at 18.4 vessels vs 68.5 historical. Diverted tonnage: 68% of crude/product tankers, 42% of dry bulk carriers, and 91% of container ships round the Cape of Good Hope. The diversion adds 12 to 18 sailing days (approx +14.5 days average) per laden voyage between Asia and Europe/Atlantic Basin, absorbing an estimated 2.8% of global dry bulk effective fleet capacity and generating a +28.4% tonne-mile expansion on Atlantic-to-Asia crude and product tanker lanes.

section_title: Panama Canal Draft Restrictions & Major Global Port Congestion Queues
section_path_text: Navigation > Chokepoints > Panama Canal & Port Queues
text: Panama Canal operations are running at 44.0 ft maximum draft in the Neo-Panamax locks with 9.8 daily transits allocated via booking auction, while Panamax locks handle 24.2 daily transits (approx 10% below peak capacity). Average auction slot waiting time is 3.8 days for unbooked vessels. Major export/import terminal congestion: Port Hedland (WAus Iron Ore) queue stands at 7.2 vessels (3.2 days wait); Tubarão (Brazil Ore) queue is 4.1 vessels (4.8 days wait); Qingdao/Caofeidian discharging delay averages 5.4 days across 18.5 Capesize vessels; Newcastle (Australia Coal) seasonal queue averages 6.2 days across 6.8 vessels. Port congestion globally immobilizes ~4.2% of Capesize and ~3.8% of Panamax on-the-water capacity.
